title: Firebase packages (Flutter)
objectives: Understand the Flutter Firebase package family + plugin architecture
Pick the right subset of firebase_* packages (don't bundle all)

sections.markdown:
**Think of `firebase_core` as the office receptionist + the other `firebase_*` packages as the specialist departments.**

`firebase_core` is the receptionist: they call your Firebase project, verify credentials, hand out badges (App instances). Every other Firebase package (`firebase_auth`, `cloud_firestore`, `firebase_messaging`, `firebase_storage`, `firebase_crashlytics`, `firebase_analytics`, `firebase_remote_config`, `firebase_performance`, `firebase_app_check`, `firebase_dynamic_links`, `firebase_in_app_messaging`, `firebase_ml_model_downloader`) then walks up to the receptionist, shows their badge, and talks to their specific service.

- **Configure via `flutterfire configure`** — CLI reads your Firebase project, downloads Android + iOS + Web config, generates `firebase_options.dart`. Manual copy-paste from the console still works but is a common source of bugs.
- **Modular** — only depend on the packages you use. Every plugin adds APK size + Play-Services glue; do NOT bundle 10 packages when you use 3.
- **Version alignment matters** — `firebase_core` version must match its Firebase BOM; all `firebase_*` packages should be on the same major line. Mismatches produce runtime crashes on Android.
- **Plugin architecture** — each package has a Dart interface (`firebase_analytics_platform_interface`) with per-platform implementations (`firebase_analytics_android`, `_ios`, `_web`) registered on startup.

**Why the plugin family exists as a set:** Firebase itself is 12+ services glued together, and each service ships its own native SDK. Rather than a monolithic 100 MB Flutter package, `flutterfire` splits per service so you install what you use.

**flutterfire** is the official family of Flutter plugins wrapping Firebase's native Android, iOS, macOS, and Web SDKs. **`firebase_core`** initializes the connection. Individual services ship as separate packages: `firebase_auth`, `cloud_firestore`, `firebase_database` (Realtime DB), `firebase_storage`, `firebase_messaging`, `firebase_crashlytics`, `firebase_analytics`, `firebase_remote_config`, `firebase_performance`, `firebase_app_check`, `firebase_dynamic_links`, `firebase_in_app_messaging`, `firebase_ml_model_downloader`, `firebase_data_connect`. **`flutterfire_cli`** automates the setup.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Manual copy-paste of `google-services.json`/`GoogleService-Info.plist`.** Easy to forget one; `flutterfire configure` writes them consistently.
**Mistake 2: Mixed package versions.** `firebase_auth 4.x` + `cloud_firestore 5.x` → native SDK conflicts on Android. Use `flutter_pub upgrade --major-versions` to keep them aligned.
**Mistake 3: Bundling every `firebase_*` package.** Each adds APK size + build time. Include only what you use.
**Mistake 4: Forgetting `Firebase.initializeApp` in a background isolate.** `firebase_messaging` background handler is a top-level function in a fresh isolate; must call `initializeApp` inside.

**Mistake 5: No emulator wiring in dev.** Every dev push touches prod Firestore + racks up cost. Wire the Emulator Suite (`useFirestoreEmulator`, `useAuthEmulator`, `useFunctionsEmulator`) behind `kDebugMode`.
**Mistake 6: Missing Android min SDK.** Modern flutterfire requires Android `minSdkVersion 21+`; older setups crash at boot.
**Mistake 7: Web SDK version drift.** `flutterfire configure` writes `firebase_options.dart` with specific Web SDK version; if you upgrade the Dart package, sometimes you need to re-run configure.

**Mistake 8: iOS `[FirebaseApp configure]` in AppDelegate + Dart `Firebase.initializeApp` both firing.** Modern flutterfire handles this; verify you don't have native init lingering from an older setup.
## Best practices
**1. Use `flutterfire configure`.** No manual JSON/plist paths.
**2. Pin `firebase_core` in `pubspec.yaml`** at the version aligned with your other firebase_*.
**3. Only depend on packages you actually use.**
**4. Wire Emulator Suite in dev** — free + safe.
**5. Environment-specific projects** — `dev`, `staging`, `prod` are separate Firebase projects with separate `firebase_options.dart` selected via `--target`.
**6. Multiple apps** — `Firebase.initializeApp(name: 'X', options: ...)` for multi-tenant / multi-Firebase-project setups.
**7. Enable App Check early** — start in debug + monitor mode; escalate to enforce.
**8. Update Dynamic Links replacement plan** — service being sunset Aug 2025; migrate to App Links / Universal Links now.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — `flutterfire configure`; verify `firebase_options.dart` + Firebase.initializeApp.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Wire Emulator Suite in dev; verify no calls hit prod.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Multi-flavor build with `dev` + `prod` Firebase projects via `--target`.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Multi-app (primary + secondary project) reading + writing to both simultaneously.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — FCM background handler initializes Firebase; verify Firestore write from background isolate.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Migrate a Dynamic Links deep-link flow to App Links / Universal Links + Firebase Hosting redirects.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: How is Firebase wired into a Flutter app in 2024+?**

**A:** Use **`flutterfire_cli`** (`dart pub global activate flutterfire_cli`) + `flutterfire configure` to pick a project + platforms. The CLI: (1) authenticates via `firebase-tools`; (2) reads / creates the Firebase project's platform apps (Android package, iOS bundle, Web app); (3) downloads / writes `google-services.json` + `GoogleService-Info.plist` + Web config; (4) generates `lib/firebase_options.dart` with `DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform`. In `main`, `await Firebase.initializeApp(options: DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform)`. Every other `firebase_*` package then just works. **Prior to flutterfire_cli**, this was a manual paste job; the CLI eliminates the #1 setup bug (mismatched configs).

**Q2: How do you manage `dev` / `staging` / `prod` Firebase projects?**

**A:** Treat each environment as a SEPARATE Firebase project (different billing, different quotas, different security rules). Options: **(1) Flavors** — Android product flavors + iOS schemes; each pulls in `firebase_options_dev.dart` vs `_prod.dart`. `flutterfire configure --project=my-dev` + `--out=lib/firebase_options_dev.dart`. Select at runtime via `--dart-define ENV=dev` + a switch in `main`. **(2) Compile-time constants** — `const env = String.fromEnvironment('ENV', defaultValue: 'dev');` picks the right options. **(3) CI matrix** — GitHub Actions job per flavor. **Why separate projects?** — one prod incident (accidental Firestore rule change, exhausted read quota) shouldn't take down dev. Also required for App Check attestation (different apps per project). Interview red flag: 'we all share one Firebase project' — instant compliance / cost / safety worry.

**Q3: How do multiple Firebase apps work + when do you need them?**

**A:** `Firebase.initializeApp(name: 'X', options: ...)` mounts a **secondary Firebase app** alongside the default. Get the specific instance via `FirebaseFirestore.instanceFor(app: secondary)`. **Use cases:** (1) **Multi-tenant SaaS** — customer-specific Firebase projects. (2) **Analytics shard** — send Analytics to one project, all other services to another (rare). (3) **Cross-org integrations** — read from partner's Firebase in a specific service. (4) **Test-in-prod builds** — a QA build reading dev + writing prod. **Gotchas:** each app has its own auth state; security rules apply per project; billing is per project. **Common mistake:** using multiple apps when a shared project + subcollections would work fine — introduces complexity for no gain. Interviewers respect a nuanced 'usually no; here's when yes.'

**Q4: How do you make Firebase testable + affordable in dev?**

**A:** **Firebase Emulator Suite** — local emulators for Auth, Firestore, RTDB, Storage, Functions, Pub/Sub, Hosting. `firebase emulators:start` boots them on localhost. In Flutter: `FirebaseFirestore.instance.useFirestoreEmulator('localhost', 8080)` behind `kDebugMode`. Also `useAuthEmulator`, `useStorageEmulator`, `useFunctionsEmulator`. **Wins:** (1) FREE — no reads billed. (2) Fast — no network round-trip. (3) Isolated — one dev's writes don't touch another's data. (4) Tests hit emulator, not prod. (5) Data seeded via `firebase emulators:start --import ./seed --export-on-exit`. **Gotchas:** emulator security rules can drift from prod — write a CI step that copies `.rules` file into the emulator + runs integration tests. **Not a substitute for staging** — emulator behavior matches prod but not perfectly (indexes, quotas).

**Q5: What does the FCM background isolate need?**

**A:** `firebase_messaging` background handlers run in a **fresh, isolated Dart isolate** — no shared globals with the main isolate. The handler MUST be: (1) a **top-level function** (not a class method or closure). (2) Marked with `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` — otherwise Flutter's tree-shaker strips it in release. (3) The FIRST thing inside is `await Firebase.initializeApp(options: DefaultFirebaseOptions.currentPlatform)` — the isolate has NO Firebase set up. Only after that can it touch Firestore / Analytics / Crashlytics. **Also:** Riverpod/Bloc/singletons in the main isolate are NOT visible; wire per-isolate access. Persist to Hive/Isar (each isolate opens its own handle) or via secure storage. **Common bug:** calling `Firestore.instance.collection('x')` in the handler without initializing → 'default Firebase App not found'.

**Q6: What's App Check and how does it fit into the flutterfire family?**

**A:** **`firebase_app_check`** attests requests come from **your legitimate app** (not a scraper or bad actor with the API key). Uses platform attestation: **Play Integrity** (Android), **DeviceCheck / App Attest** (iOS), **reCAPTCHA v3 / Enterprise** (Web). The SDK acquires an attestation token; Firebase services (Firestore, Storage, Functions) reject requests without valid tokens once you flip them to enforcement. **Setup:** (1) install the package; (2) `FirebaseAppCheck.instance.activate(...)` in `main`; (3) enable in Firebase console; (4) initially set to 'monitor mode' — real requests logged but not blocked; (5) once monitor shows attested traffic is legitimate, flip to enforcement. **Cost:** minor CPU + network at startup; free tier is generous. **Why every serious app should have it:** free protection against API-key abuse + cost-attack floods + credential stuffing.

## Real-world usage

- **Almost every consumer Flutter app** — auth + Firestore or FCM at minimum.
- **Enterprise** — Auth + Firestore + Analytics + Crashlytics + Remote Config is a standard 5-plugin bundle.
- **Multi-env** — separate projects per flavor.
- **Dev loop** — emulator suite + local `.rules` + seeded data.
- **NOT ideal for** — apps with strict data-residency requirements that Firebase's regions don't meet.

## Advanced notes

- **`firebase_options.dart` under source control** — YES; contains non-secret identifiers (project id, API key) that are safe to publish.
- **Multi-flavor with `--out=lib/firebase_options_{{flavor}}.dart`** — flag on `flutterfire configure`.
- **iOS deep-linking bundles** — Firebase Dynamic Links being sunset in Aug 2025; migrate to Universal Links + your own resolver.
- **`firebase_data_connect`** — new package wrapping a Postgres-backed API surface.
- **Web-specific SDK version pinning** — `firebase_options.dart` sets the CDN SDK version; test after Dart-side upgrades.
- **Android Play Integrity setup** — enable in Play Console + Firebase console; App Check consumes it.
- **Firestore offline persistence** — enabled by default on mobile; explicitly `settings = Settings(persistenceEnabled: false)` to disable.
- **Multi-DB Firestore** — new feature: multiple Firestore databases per project via `FirebaseFirestore.instanceFor(app, databaseId: 'analytics')`.
- **`firebase.json` (Hosting) at repo root** — for hosting rewrite rules alongside Flutter Web deploys.
- **iOS 17 permissions** — modern Info.plist entries required for Auth phone + FCM + Analytics IDFA.
- **Version alignment** — the FlutterFire docs page tracks pairwise-compatible versions.
